title: Shared Team AI Agent — Typed, Executable Admin Configuration API
assumptions: Northstar Consulting has three seeded members: John, Mary, and Bob. John is the only administrator; Mary and Bob are regular members. The role seed/migration is idempotent and updates existing John records, so a pre-existing SQLite database cannot retain a stale member role.

The browser must treat the server's explicit capability flag as authoritative for admin-panel visibility; it must not infer administration rights from a display name, a cached profile, or a hard-coded user ID.
Agent configuration is team-scoped and stored in SQLite. It applies to every current and future member of the team on the next chat completion.
Only John may add, change, test, enable, or remove configuration. The server, not browser JavaScript, resolves the active configuration fresh for every model turn.

Configuration can include administrator-authored prompt text, uploaded Markdown reference documents, uploaded SKILL.md instruction bundles, HTTP function tools, and remote MCP servers. Each configured capability has a stable ID, enabled state, and audit timestamps.

External tools and MCP servers are real runtime capabilities: enabled definitions are supplied to the live LLM request, model-requested calls are persisted as execution records, and their results are supplied back to the model before the final assistant answer. Demo mode must clearly state that it cannot execute external capabilities.

Conversation records persist last_activity_at. On an existing database migration, it is backfilled from the newest persisted message timestamp, falling back to created_at for empty conversations; no private message or conversation is discarded.

authorization.session: Every API endpoint except login and health requires an unexpired session cookie.
authorization.admin_configuration: Every /api/admin/configuration* endpoint requires the current session user to have role admin. A non-admin receives 403. Team and editor identity always derive from the session, never request data.
authorization.execution_visibility: All users may read only execution records belonging to their own private conversation. An admin may additionally inspect team-scoped execution diagnostics only when a dedicated audit endpoint is added; no cross-user private prompt or tool arguments are exposed by default.
authorization.regular_member_visibility: Regular members do not receive editable admin configuration payloads or admin UI. Configuration is server-applied to their LLM completion requests. They may approve only a pending external call from their own conversation.

endpoints.notes: The returned user.role and capabilities.admin_configuration are required fields for every successful login.
The client refreshes this identity after login and must use capabilities.admin_configuration to show or hide the admin entry point.

conversations contains only the signed-in user's conversations, ordered by last_activity_at descending, then id descending. capabilities duplicates the current authenticated identity capability deliberately, allowing a newly mounted UI to make the access decision from the bootstrap response even if its local identity state was cleared.
Returns only the signed-in user's private conversations, ordered by last_activity_at descending, then id descending. It is the authoritative refresh endpoint after a message changes recency.

endpoints.notes: For a live provider, the server sends enabled HTTP function definitions and enabled MCP server definitions as provider tools, plus bounded enabled Markdown/SKILL.md/prompt instructions. It validates and executes requested HTTP calls server-side, stores each result, then continues the provider response loop until it produces the final assistant message or needs approval. Every continuation after a capability result resends the complete resolved system instructions. A 201 completed turn contains an assistant message grounded in the persisted capability result(s), never transient tool-progress narration. The returned conversation is the authoritative row after these updates; clients move/retain it at the top of their rail without a full reload.

side_effects: approved=true resumes the paused MCP/tool execution and model loop
approved=false marks the execution rejected and returns that result to the model so it can answer without the call

behavior.role_enforcement: The server stores roles in the users table and includes the role label plus the derived admin_configuration capability in every authenticated identity and bootstrap response. Hiding admin controls is not authorization; every configuration route enforces role on the server. The client must show the entry point exactly when capabilities.admin_configuration is true, then keep the API 403 as the security boundary.
behavior.admin_discovery: If an authenticated John response lacks role=admin or capabilities.admin_configuration=true, the client treats it as an identity/bootstrap error, displays a retryable notice, and does not silently render a member UI. This makes a stale server image, stale database migration, or schema mismatch diagnosable instead of appearing as a missing panel.
behavior.conversation_ordering: The conversation rail is recency-first. Both bootstrap and GET /api/conversations filter by the session's team and user, then sort by last_activity_at descending with id descending as the deterministic tie-breaker. A newly created empty conversation uses its creation timestamp as activity; a message request moves its conversation to the top immediately, including when a provider response is still awaiting approval.
behavior.conversation_activity_migration: Startup adds a nullable last_activity_at column when absent, backfills each legacy conversation with MAX(messages.created_at) or its created_at, then enforces a non-null value for new rows and creates a team/user/activity index. Until a deployment completes that backfill, reads use COALESCE(last_activity_at, created_at) so ordering remains safe. If migration cannot commit atomically, startup fails and the API returns 500 rather than serving an ambiguously ordered partial schema.
behavior.long_conversation_loading: The UI initially requests one newest MessagePage and renders only that bounded page. At the scroll container's top edge it may fetch the next older page; before prepending, it captures scrollHeight and scrollTop and restores scrollTop by the height increase. Concurrent page requests are deduplicated, a failed older-page fetch leaves existing messages interactive, and a newly sent message is appended without reloading the full history. This prevents DOM growth, expensive innerHTML rebuilds, and jumps that can make a long chat appear frozen or unscrollable.
behavior.configuration_propagation: A message completion loads the configuration and revision fresh from SQLite for the session user's team. It uses the same configuration for John, Mary, and Bob; no browser-provided configuration is trusted. Every turn and execution record carries the resolved revision for auditability.
behavior.instruction_composition: The immutable privacy, authorization, and team-memory rules remain first. The current admin textarea is appended as team policy, followed by bounded enabled prompt-template text, Markdown documents, and SKILL.md instruction bundles clearly delimited as administrator-managed reference data. Every enabled template applies globally to every user's next provider request; templates are not user-owned, selected per-browser, or executable. Uploaded Markdown is not loaded from the server filesystem or executed. None of this content can override immutable rules, request secrets, or grant itself tool access.
behavior.http_function_runtime: For each enabled HttpFunctionTool, the live provider receives a function tool definition containing its name, description, and input_schema, but never its endpoint headers or environment-variable references. On a provider function call, the server verifies the capability remains enabled in the turn's revision, validates arguments against input_schema, creates an AgentToolExecution, resolves permitted server-side headers, invokes the configured HTTPS endpoint with a short timeout and redirect disabled, bounds/redacts the response, persists the result, and supplies a function-call-result item back to the provider. It repeats this bounded loop until a final answer, an approval request, or failure. The server never lets model arguments select a host, scheme, arbitrary header, file path, or executable.
behavior.mcp_runtime: For every enabled, validated RemoteMcpServer, the live provider receives only the configured remote MCP descriptor, allowlisted tool names, and approval policy. Calls outside allowed_tools are rejected and recorded even if a remote server advertises them. For approval_policy=always, an AgentToolExecution is persisted as awaiting_approval and the turn returns 202; only the owner of that private conversation can approve or reject it. For policy=never, the server/provider may continue automatically. MCP call outputs and failures are persisted as bounded, redacted results and returned to the model loop before the final answer.
behavior.provider_continuations: After every HTTP-function or MCP capability call, including a rejected or failed call represented as a tool result, the server creates the next provider request with the same complete resolved system instructions used for the initial turn: immutable rules, current team configuration revision, enabled prompt templates, Markdown, and SKILL.md content. Supplying only a prior response ID or only tool output is insufficient. The server preserves the bounded prior conversation and persisted tool-result items needed for continuity.
behavior.post_capability_answer: When a completed 201 turn follows one or more capability calls, its assistant_message must be concise and grounded only in the persisted returned result(s) plus already-authorized user question context. It must not expose chain-of-thought, implementation traces, polling/progress narration, or claim a call succeeded when its execution record did not. It names the capability accurately as an HTTP function or an MCP tool/server, rather than conflating the two. For GitHub issue results, it lists each returned issue title and canonical URL when present; when the returned issue count is zero, it explicitly says that no matching issues were found. A GitHub issue request must not add label filters unless the user explicitly requested those labels.
behavior.completion_audit_invariant: For every 201 AgentTurn with capability activity, each provider-requested call has exactly one persisted AgentToolExecution linked to the turn's conversation and resolved configuration revision, with terminal state succeeded, failed, rejected, or a documented terminal timeout. The final assistant message is persisted only after its corresponding capability result records exist. The response's turn.executions and assistant_message therefore provide an auditable, user-visible summary without exposing raw provider reasoning.
behavior.external_data_and_security: External results are untrusted data, not model instructions. Requests and results use size, timeout, and call-count bounds. All configured URLs must use HTTPS and must be rejected if they resolve to loopback, link-local, private, multicast, or reserved network ranges; redirects, raw secrets, cookie forwarding, and arbitrary request headers are prohibited. Environment variable references are allowlisted by deployment configuration and are never serialized in normal user responses. The app does not expose a user conversation, session cookie, private history, or team-memory corpus to a tool/MCP server unless the configured schema/call explicitly carries an administrator-approved input field.
behavior.failure_handling: A failed, timed-out, invalid, disabled, or rejected external call becomes an execution record with a safe error and a tool-result response to the model where possible. It is not silently represented as successful. A failure that prevents a coherent final response returns the documented 502/504 without losing the user's already-persisted message.
